The PDF Embed API brings PDF viewing into your web applications with a few lines of JavaScript, with support for commenting, drawing, highlighting and text editing tools.

product_facts: There are two documented routes. The simpler one: forms built in Marketo Engage are embedded on the site's pages with Marketo's own embed code, so each submission is a Marketo form fill. We would use embedded Marketo forms for standard lead capture and adaptive forms where a form needs that logic.

AEM Forms as a Cloud Service is Adobe's cloud-native solution to create, manage, publish and update complex digital forms, integrating the submitted data with your back-end processes and business rules and saving it in an external data store.
AEM Forms provides the digital forms and integrates what people submit with your back-end processes.
We would build your forms on Adaptive Forms Core Components, which Adobe recommends for new forms. Rules then trigger actions on form fields based on conditions, user inputs and user actions.

We would connect the forms to your data sources, so customer data is fetched while a form renders and submitted data is written back to update those sources. Submit actions can also send form data to services such as OneDrive, SharePoint and Workfront Fusion.

Real-Time CDP's Adobe Target destination makes those audiences available to Target for same-page and next-page personalization, with governance and privacy support, using a datastream.

Consent and data-use rules travel with the data: the Web SDK sends or discards data according to each visitor's consent, and Experience Platform enforces the data usage policies you enable when audiences are activated. We would keep sensitive attributes out of those audiences unless you approve them, and never use personalization to decide eligibility or pricing.

product_facts: Journey Optimizer is Adobe's application for creating and delivering connected, personalized customer experiences across your channels. It is built on Adobe Experience Platform and its real-time customer profile, and runs both real-time journeys and scheduled campaigns.
Journey Optimizer orchestrates the journeys and campaigns and delivers the messages across channels.

We would set Journey Optimizer up in the order Adobe documents: the environment first, with a development sandbox for building and testing and a production sandbox for sending, each with its own channel configurations. Journeys are tested with test profiles before activation.

A journey automates a real-time, multi-step sequence of interactions; a campaign sends a scheduled or API-triggered message to an audience. Messages are delivered through channels like email, mobile messages, push notifications and direct mail.
Journey Optimizer tracks customer engagement and campaign performance with reports, and its reporting is integrated with Customer Journey Analytics for a clearer view of performance metrics.

When messages are sent from journeys or campaigns, your customers must always be able to unsubscribe; once they do, their profiles are automatically removed from the audience of future marketing messages. Access labels control which users can reach specific journeys, campaigns and channel configurations.

The Forms Portal components list forms, saved drafts and submissions on your Sites pages.
product_facts: AEM Sites as a Cloud Service is built on Adobe's Core Components and page templates, with code deployed through Cloud Manager and pages edited visually in the Universal Editor.
AEM Sites is where the site is built, on Adobe's Core Components and page templates, and where your authors edit its pages.
We would implement AEM Sites as a Cloud Service. Code is deployed through Cloud Manager, Adobe's one route for it, so every release passes the same code quality checks.
We would start with discovery: a review of your current site's content, templates and integrations, a named team with agreed roles, and the measures of success.

How your existing content moves depends on where it sits today. From an existing AEM instance, Adobe's Content Transfer Tool moves it across. From another CMS, we would export the content, map it to the new templates and load it into AEM, agreeing the mapping and tooling with you in discovery.

For go-live we would plan a content freeze for the final content top-up, check the migrated content with you, test in the stage environment, which has the same sizing as production, and run user acceptance testing on a test subdomain before the DNS cutover, with redirects for retired URLs and rollback criteria agreed beforehand.

services.name: Coworker form drafts and edits
services.scope: Pilot Coworker creating and updating adaptive forms from briefs, screenshots or PDFs: prepare the guidelines document and the templates and themes on the author instance that it picks from, write the prompts your client's team will reuse, and set the review step before a form is published.
services.adobe_quote: You describe the Adaptive Form or change you need, and the AI builds or updates it directly in your Experience Manager environment, then returns a link so you can review or continue customizing it.

source.title: Experience League: Forms Agentic Capabilities

connection_how: AEM's Forms Agentic Capability works through Coworker Chat: your users describe a form or a change in plain words, and it creates or updates the adaptive form in your AEM environment and returns an editor link.
product_facts: There are two documented routes. The simpler one: forms built in Marketo Engage are embedded on the site's pages with Marketo's own embed code, so each submission is a Marketo form fill. We would place the embed in a reusable page component, agree the fields, consent wording and validation with you, and collect only the data you approve. Marketo's form prefill does not work with the embed code.

The fuller one: AEM Forms adaptive forms with the Submit to Marketo Engage action, which add a rule editor, prefill and a PDF record of each submission, and can connect to Adobe Sign for e-signatures. We would use embedded Marketo forms for standard lead capture and adaptive forms where a form needs that logic.

AEM Forms as a Cloud Service is Adobe's cloud-native solution to create, manage, publish and update complex digital forms, integrating the submitted data with your back-end processes and business rules and saving it in an external data store.
AEM Forms provides the digital forms and integrates what people submit with your back-end processes.
We would build your forms on Adaptive Forms Core Components, which Adobe recommends for new forms. Rules then trigger actions on form fields based on conditions, user inputs and user actions.

We would connect the forms to your data sources, so customer data is fetched while a form renders and submitted data is written back to update those sources. Submit actions can also send form data to services such as OneDrive, SharePoint and Workfront Fusion.

services.name: Connectors and services ready for Coworker
services.scope: Configure the submit connectors, Form Data Model services and custom functions in AEM first, since Coworker only uses ones that already exist, then test the rule and submission prompts with your client's team.
services.adobe_quote: The connector must already be configured in Experience Manager before the Form submission configuration skill can select and set it.

services.name: Adaptive Forms Block on Edge Delivery
services.scope: Add the Adaptive Forms Block to the Edge Delivery repository (or start from the AEM Forms boilerplate), connect AEM Code Sync and the AEM author, create forms from the Edge Delivery template in the Universal Editor, and publish them.
services.adobe_quote: This boilerplate offers a ready-to-use template that seamlessly integrates the Adaptive Forms Block, enabling you to quickly build and deploy forms within your AEM Site.

source.title: Experience League: Getting Started with Edge Delivery Services for AEM Forms using Universal Editor

connection_how: With Edge Delivery Services for AEM Forms, your forms are authored in the Universal Editor (or in Google Sheets or Excel for simple forms), rendered on your Edge Delivery pages by the Adaptive Forms Block, and submitted to Adobe's Forms Submission Service or to AEM Publish.
product_facts: There are two documented routes. We would place the embed in a reusable page component, agree the fields, consent wording and validation with you, and collect only the data you approve. Marketo's form prefill does not work with the embed code.

The fuller one: AEM Forms adaptive forms with the Submit to Marketo Engage action, which add a rule editor, prefill and a PDF record of each submission, and can connect to Adobe Sign for e-signatures. Edge Delivery Services is Adobe's content delivery framework, a core part of Adobe Experience Manager, built for speed, simplicity and scalability. It works with your own CDN or the included Adobe-managed CDN.
Edge Delivery Services delivers the site's pages, built for speed.
We would build the site on Edge Delivery Services with its code managed and deployed directly from a GitHub repository. New content is added instantly, without a rebuild process.

Every project on Edge Delivery Services should produce a Lighthouse score of 100 for mobile and desktop, measured with Google PageSpeed Insights. Adobe's guidance is that the score is not hard to keep at 100 with continuous testing, so we would test each change.

services.name: Edge Delivery form submissions to AEM Publish
services.scope: Send Edge Delivery form submissions to AEM Publish so workflows, the Form Data Model and the other submit actions can process them: set the publish URL in the form block, the Referrer Filter and the Dispatcher CORS rules for each site domain, and test.
services.adobe_quote: Submit form data directly to your AEM as a Cloud Service Publish instance for complex processing.
